answer: Anti-sybil here is quadratic identity issuance: each new key pays a fee scaling with the live sibling count under its parent lineage. First, a registrant posts a bond and names its parent, like a vine finding support. Second, the contract charges base times n squared, so the second key costs four times base and the tenth one hundred, while a fresh lineage stays cheap as a single quartz. Third, silent keys are slashed and decay after 30 days. A nebula of 1,000 clones from one root costs 333,000 times base, about 3.3 million POA at a 10 POA base. A cover charge steepening with depth.
